The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(v_p(n)\) be the exponent of prime \(p\) in \(n\).

When Mark replaces \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b)\) and \(\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), for every prime \(p\), the two exponents \(v_p(a),v_p(b)\) are replaced by their minimum and maximum. Thus, for each prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

At the end, no move changes the board. If two numbers were incomparable under divisibility, replacing them by their gcd and lcm would change the board. So the final board must form a divisibility chain.

Sort the final board as
\[
N_1 \le N_2 \le \cdots \le N_{2100}.
\]
For each prime \(p\), the sequence
\[
v_p(N_1)\le v_p(N_2)\le \cdots \le v_p(N_{2100})
\]
is a nondecreasing arrangement of the invariant multiset of \(p\)-exponents from \(1,2,\dots,2100\). Hence \(v_p(N_i)\) is the \(i\)-th smallest value among
\[
v_p(1),v_p(2),\dots,v_p(2100).
\]

We need \(N_{2026}\). Since \(2100-2026+1=75\), this is the 75th entry from the top. For a fixed prime \(p\), the number of integers \(n\le 2100\) with \(v_p(n)\ge t\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t} \right\rfloor.
\]
Thus \(v_p(N_{2026})\ge t\) iff
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t} \right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Since \(2100/75=28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^t\le 28.
\]
Therefore
\[
N_{2026}=\prod_p p^{\max\{t:p^t\le 28\}}
=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28).
\]

Now
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,28)
=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
